{{Short description|Theorem in complex analysis about the sheaf of holomorphic functions}}

In [[mathematics]], specifically [[algebraic geometry]], the '''Oka coherence theorem''', proved by [[Kiyoshi Oka]] in 1950,{{sfnp|Oka|1950}} states that the [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]] <math>\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^n}</math> of  [[holomorphic function]]s on <math>\mathbb{C}^n</math> (and subsequently the sheaf <math>\mathcal{O}_{X}</math> of holomorphic functions on a [[complex manifold]] <math>X</math>) is [[coherent sheaf|coherent]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Noguchi|2019}}</ref><ref>In {{harvtxt|Oka|1950}} it was called the ''[[idéal de domaines indéterminés]]''.</ref>
